theory.title: Wish e if only para situaciones presentes
theory.explanation: Usa wish + pasado simple para expresar que algo del presente te gustaría que fuera diferente. If only añade énfasis. Para capacidades, usa wish + could; para comportamientos repetidos, wish + would.
theory.tip: Wish + pasado simple expresa un deseo sobre el presente; wish + could habla de una capacidad.

content.passage: After another small disagreement, Ella told her brother that she wished they had more time to talk. If only they listened to each other before getting annoyed, she said, things would be easier. Her brother admitted that he sometimes reacted too quickly. He wished he could stay calm when plans changed. They agreed to make an effort and discuss problems earlier. Neither expected everything to change overnight, but both wanted to improve the way they communicated.

items.prompt: Describe a relationship that is important to you.
items.modelAnswer: One relationship that matters to me is the one I have with my younger brother. We have different interests, but we make time to have dinner together every Sunday. That routine helps us stay close even when work gets busy.

items.prompt: Explain how you would deal with a misunderstanding.
items.modelAnswer: If I realised someone had misunderstood me, I would contact them as soon as possible. I would explain what I meant, listen to their reaction and apologise if my words caused confusion. I wouldn't try to solve it through a long chain of messages.

items.prompt: Talk about a custom you have learned from another culture.
items.modelAnswer: At a cultural exchange evening, I learned that in some countries people remove their shoes before entering a home. I found it interesting because it shows respect for the host and keeps the house clean. Now I always check local customs when I travel.

items.prompt: Describe how you stay in touch with people who live far away.
items.modelAnswer: I keep in touch with friends abroad through video calls and voice messages. We cannot always speak at the same time because of work and time differences, so we send updates during the week and arrange a longer call at weekends.

items.prompt: Give advice to someone who wants to improve a friendship.
items.modelAnswer: I would suggest planning something simple together, such as a walk or a coffee, rather than waiting for a special occasion. I would also ask my friend what they need instead of assuming. Regular attention can improve a friendship.

items.prompt: Explain what you wish people did more often when communicating.
items.modelAnswer: I wish people listened without interrupting so often. Sometimes someone needs to explain a problem before receiving advice. I also wish people asked follow-up questions, because that shows they are interested and have understood.

items.prompt: Describe a disagreement and how it was resolved.
items.modelAnswer: My colleague and I disagreed about how to organise a presentation. I wanted to use slides, while she preferred a short demonstration. We combined both ideas and asked another teammate for feedback. The final presentation was clearer and more engaging.

items.prompt: Compare two ways of keeping in contact.
items.modelAnswer: Text messages are convenient for quick information, while video calls are better for emotional or complicated topics. I use messages to arrange plans, but I prefer a call when I haven't spoken to someone for a long time.

items.prompt: Explain how you make your messages clear and polite.
items.modelAnswer: I make messages clearer by putting the main point near the beginning and using short paragraphs. I check names, dates and attachments before sending an email. If I need an answer, I include a polite question and a clear deadline.

items.prompt: Summarise what makes communication successful.
items.modelAnswer: Successful communication starts with knowing what you want to say and considering who will receive the message. It also requires listening, asking questions and checking that the other person has understood. The best method depends on the situation.
